articles.title: Jolie Revolutionizes Showerheads as Luxury Item
articles.summary: Jolie has successfully elevated the status of showerheads through its innovative approach, making them a desirable conversation piece in the world of beauty and wellness.
articles.content: A revolutionary shift has taken place in the world of beauty and wellness, with one company transforming a humble showerhead into a coveted luxury item. Jolie, a brand that started out as an underdog, has successfully elevated the status of a once-overlooked bathroom fixture, turning it into a must-have product for those seeking to upgrade their daily routine. Through its innovative approach, Jolie has managed to make the showerhead a desirable conversation piece, with a range of collaborations and creative initiatives that have brought attention to this often-neglected area of personal grooming. The brand's success can be measured by its impressive revenue projections, with estimates suggesting it will generate $65 million in 2026 - a significant milestone for a company that has built a multi-million-dollar business around a single product. Jolie's latest innovation is the Filtered Handheld Showerhead, set to be released on November 11, and available in five distinct colorways, including Modern Chrome, Brushed Gold, and Vibrant Red. The new handheld showerhead boasts a sleek design with a knurled aluminium handle and magnetic docking system, allowing it to snap seamlessly into place - a testament to the brand's commitment to style as well as functionality. As Jolie continues to disrupt the traditional beauty industry, its founder is looking to expand the brand's product offerings beyond its flagship showerhead. This move comes on the heels of a series of successful campaigns that have successfully repositioned the shower as a space for self-care and intimacy. One such campaign was a partnership with 831 Stories, a romance publisher, which saw Jolie team up with them to create an Instagram series pairing steamy reads with hot showers. This unique collaboration brought together two seemingly disparate worlds, showcasing the versatility of Jolie's products in a new light. In addition to this partnership, Jolie also made waves during Copenhagen Fashion Week by installing showers along the city's harbor for swimmers. This innovative move not only highlighted the brand's commitment to style and functionality but also brought its products into a public setting that combined art with function. The brand has also been making headlines with its editorial series, "Shower Thoughts, which draws inspiration from the bathroom. The series features video interviews with creatives who have built something of their own, reflecting Jolie's ties to fashion, design, art, and culture. Filmed in and around guests' bathrooms, the series offers a unique glimpse into the lives of these individuals, highlighting the ways in which they incorporate self-care and ritual into their daily routines. First-season guests include Vyrao founder Yasmin Sewell and fashion designer Mara Hoffman, among others. The success of these campaigns has positioned Jolie as a leader in the beauty industry, with its focus on redefining the traditional shower experience. As the brand continues to evolve and expand, it's clear that its commitment to style and functionality will remain at its core. To establish its brand, Jolie first needed to create a market for itself by educating consumers about the benefits of filtered shower water. The company's founder had confidence in his product from the start, but he knew that convincing people to install it themselves and filtering their shower water would be a significant challenge. Jolie addressed this issue by licensing publicly available data on water quality and creating a free local water report that allows users to enter their email address and zip code to receive information about the contaminants in their water. This initiative, dubbed step zero, enables Jolie to explain the potential impact of unfiltered shower water on skin and hair, providing a clear rationale for why its product is necessary. The brand's focus on addressing hair concerns has led to significant growth and expansion. Jolie expects to report between $11 million and $12 million in EBITDA for 2026, a notable increase from previous years. To put this growth into perspective, the company has processed over two million Shopify orders for showerheads and replacement filters since 2021. This impressive figure is a testament to the brand's ability to meet customer demand and provide a solution to common hair problems. The subscription model has proven to be a key component of Jolie's success, with about 75% of first-time buyers opting to receive a new filter every quarter. The brand retains around 80% of these subscribers at the end of their first year, demonstrating its ability to build long-term relationships with customers. The response to Sacred Water, the second product from Jolie's brand, was more mixed than the first one. While some praised its innovative design, others criticized it online, even making it a topic of discussion on late-night TV shows like Jimmy Kimmel Live. Despite this polarized reaction, Babenzien sees the partnership as an opportunity to build long-term relationships with customers. He views Jolie's brand through a lens that prioritizes building a connection with its audience rather than solely focusing on revenue generation. Erewhon, a high-end grocery store chain, played a significant role in introducing Jolie's wellness proposition to a broader retail audience. articles.title: Duke Men's Basketball Team Suffers Crushing Defeat to Michigan State
articles.summary: The Duke men's basketball team lost 79-73 to Michigan State in the Champions Classic game, with concerns arising about the Blue Devils' performance and expectations for the season.
articles.content: Duke University's men's basketball team suffered a crushing defeat at the hands of Michigan State, losing 79-73 in the Champions Classic game. The loss has sparked concerns about Duke's performance and whether it is time to reassess expectations for the Blue Devils this season. Head coach Jon Scheyer was visibly frustrated after the game, taking aim at several aspects of his team's play. He expressed dissatisfaction with the guard play, connectivity, toughness, and overall shooting. The usually composed and level-headed coach seemed particularly peeved about the team's inability to work together effectively on offense. Duke struggled to get into a rhythm, managing just 0.75 points per possession in the first half. Michigan State, on the other hand, looked cohesive and well-coordinated throughout the game. National player of the year candidate Jeremy Fears Jr. was instrumental in his team's success, dominating the court from start to finish. The Blue Devils' offense was a disjointed mess, with players frequently going one-on-one against the defense instead of working together to create scoring opportunities. Coach Scheyer acknowledged that his team needs to improve its ability to fight for the rim and seek better shot options. The loss has undoubtedly been a wake-up call for Duke as it looks to bounce back in its next game. The Blue Devils' defense struggled to contain Michigan State's offense, which was fueled by sophomore wing Jordan Scott's impressive performance on both ends of the court. Scott's athleticism and length were on full display as he racked up nine rebounds and swatted six shots. Michigan State's forward Cam Ward praised Scott's defensive prowess, stating that "Jordan is the X factor on defense" due to his ability to be everywhere on the court at all times. The Spartans' defense was a key factor in their win, with Scott leading the way. Michigan State's success can be attributed to its tried-and-true formula of physical play, high-level point guard play, and toughness. This approach has been the hallmark of the program for over two decades, as evident from their past performances in slobberknocker games like this one. The Spartans have a talented young core that could make some noise in March. Duke's struggles at the point guard position were evident, with Cayden Boozer and Caleb Foster failing to leave their mark on the game. Boozer played only nine minutes in the second half, while Foster shot poorly from the field, including several ill-advised shots. Michigan State's John Blackwell had a productive night despite the Spartans' early lead, finishing with 17 points thanks to a late-game surge. However, it was clear that Duke's offense was not at its best, and coach Scheyer will likely look to make adjustments in their next game. Duke's offense struggled to find its rhythm against Michigan State, a trend that coach Scheyer will likely look to address in their next game. The Blue Devils' perimeter play was particularly underwhelming, with none of their guards standing out on the night. This lackluster performance highlights the need for improvement from Duke's backcourt players. Joaquim Boumtje-Boumtje, a highly touted prospect, had a relatively quiet game, scoring only five points and grabbing four rebounds. His struggles with his jumper were evident, but coach Scheyer remains optimistic about his potential impact on the team. Coach Scheyer emphasized the importance of putting Joaquim in better positions to score and also highlighted the need for him to develop other skills such as defense and rebounding. He praised the young player's competitiveness and willingness to learn from the experience. As Duke looks to bounce back, they will likely focus on making adjustments to their offense and finding ways to get Joaquim more involved in the game. Coach Scheyer believes that with continued growth and development, the 17-year-old prospect will become a valuable asset to the team. The Blue Devils' struggles against Michigan State have sparked a re-evaluation of their prospects this season. The team's performance has left many questioning whether they are on track to meet initial expectations. Coach Scheyer is now tasked with revisiting his lineup and strategy in search of a more balanced approach that incorporates shooting and teamwork, rather than relying on individual stars. With the NBA draft looming, Boumtje Boumtje will have to wait for better days as he continues to develop his skills. articles.title: Kennedy Family Members File to Intervene in Lawsuit Against Trump's Arch
articles.summary: A group of nine Kennedy family members has filed a request in a Washington federal court to intervene in the lawsuit against President Donald Trump's planned arch on the nation's capital, citing concerns over its impact on gravesites and memorials.
articles.content: A group of nine Kennedy family members has filed a request in a Washington federal court to intervene in the lawsuit against President Donald Trump's planned arch on the nation's capital. The move comes as part of an ongoing dispute between the Kennedys and Trump over various issues. The Kennedy family members argue that the proposed location of the arch would cast a shadow over some gravesites, including those belonging to their relatives. They also claim that the structure would obstruct the line of sight from the John F. Kennedy Eternal Flame memorial across the Arlington Memorial Bridge to the Lincoln Memorial, which they consider an integral part of its design. This is not the first time the Kennedy family has clashed with Trump over a project; they have previously opposed his attempt to add his name to the Kennedy Center and were also critical when he decided to close the institution due to a court ruling. The Kennedy family's opposition to President Trump's proposed monument has led them to take legal action against the project. The arch, set to be built on Memorial Circle in Washington, would stand at 250 feet tall, significantly taller than the Lincoln Memorial. A federal judge recently blocked construction of the arch after a planning board with ties to the president voted to approve it. This move has sparked concerns about the monument's impact on Arlington National Cemetery and the surrounding area. The Kennedy family has long been protective of this hallowed ground. The proposed arch would not only cast shadows over graves, but also undermine democratic principles by ignoring safeguards put in place to protect the site. The family's opposition is just the latest example of their disagreement with President Trump's vision for Washington. The construction of President Trump's proposed memorial arch at Arlington National Cemetery has sparked opposition from some members of the Kennedy family, who have intervened in the ongoing lawsuit against the project. Notably, several prominent Kennedys are buried at Arlington, including President John F. Kennedy and his wife Jacqueline Onassis. The Kennedy family members arguing against the construction cite their unique interest in protecting the gravesites of their loved ones. In court documents, they emphasized that as members of the Kennedy family, they have a particular stake in ensuring that these graves remain unimpeded as a solemn tribute to their family's legacy. In response to the Kennedy family's opposition, a spokesperson for the memorial arch project stated that it is unfortunate to see some family members joining the litigation against the arch. The project aims to honor those who rest at Arlington Cemetery, including the Kennedy family members buried there.
